question: Which entry on 3.1.32 yields a CJK-capable font for the v8 Manager labels?
prototype_hypothesis: miwear_font_create(index, size) picks the family from a fixed table and forwards to lvx_font_create(name, size, 0); entries 4-6 are the MiSansF-* (full) families, while the font_config.json family list only knows MiSans-Demibold/Semibold/Medium/Regular.
callsite_evidence: 0xc4bd728 miwear_font_create(index, size): r4 = off_2C70E6BC[index], then lvx_font_create(r4, size, 0); on failure logs 'failed to creat miwear font' and returns LV_FONT_DEFAULT.
off_2C70E6BC = MiSans-Demibold, MiSans-Medium, MiSans-Regular, MiSans-Demibold, MiSansF-Demibold, MiSansF-Medium, MiSansF-Semibold.
Stock font setup at 0xc395286 calls miwear_font_create(4, 0x66) and 0xc39529c miwear_font_create(4, 0x5A), i.e. index 4 is the family used for large display text.
The romfs font config lists only the four MiSans-* families, so MiSansF-* is reachable only through this table.
A Manager page on 3.1.32 renders its rows but every CJK glyph is .notdef when the label font comes from lvx_font_create('MiSans-Regular', 14/18, 0) or from LV_FONT_DEFAULT.
control_flow_evidence: The returned font is applied to a label as local style property 90, the same setter the Manager backend already uses.
ownership_analysis: No ownership claimed; the font object belongs to the firmware font manager.
unsafe_assumptions: Index 4 (MiSansF-Demibold) is assumed to carry CJK at body sizes; the index for the stock body text has not been identified.
Static evidence only; the device run that would confirm CJK rendering has not been recorded yet.
recommended_probe: Build the n66 Supervisor with the miwear_font_create mapping and confirm the Manager page draws Chinese instead of .notdef boxes.
